items.q: What is the recognized cut-off value for endometrial thickness on transvaginal ultrasound in a postmenopausal woman presenting with vaginal bleeding, below which endometrial cancer is extremely unlikely (< 1%)?
items.exp: Extensive prospective international multicenter studies have confirmed that a transvaginal ultrasound endometrial stripe thickness <= 4 mm in a woman with postmenopausal bleeding has a negative predictive value > 99% for endometrial carcinoma. Biopsy is indicated when thickness exceeds 4 mm.
r: Correct. Endometrial thickness <= 4 mm in postmenopausal bleeding has a > 99% negative predictive value for malignancy.
Incorrect. 8 mm is abnormal in postmenopause and carries a high risk of cancer.
Incorrect. 12 mm represents marked thickening requiring urgent biopsy.
Incorrect. 15 mm is massively thickened.
items.kp: An endometrial stripe thickness <= 4 mm on ultrasound in postmenopausal bleeding has a > 99% negative predictive value for cancer.

items.q: Under the Bokhman classification of endometrial cancer, which genetic alteration is characteristic of Type I endometrioid adenocarcinoma?
o: Inactivating mutation of the PTEN tumor suppressor gene
items.exp: Bokhman Type I endometrioid endometrial carcinomas are estrogen-dependent and characteristically harbor inactivating mutations of the PTEN tumor suppressor gene (present in 60-80% of cases), along with PIK3CA, KRAS, and microsatellite instability (MSI). TP53 mutations and HER2 amplification characterize aggressive Type II serous carcinomas.
r: Correct. PTEN mutation is the signature genetic alteration in Type I endometrioid carcinoma.
Incorrect. TP53 mutations define Type II serous carcinoma (> 90%).
Incorrect. HER2 amplification is found in Type II serous tumors.
Incorrect. BRCA1 mutations are linked to ovarian and breast cancer, not Type I endometrial cancer.
items.kp: Type I endometrioid endometrial carcinoma is characterized by PTEN tumor suppressor gene inactivation.

items.q: A 44-year-old woman with newly diagnosed endometrial adenocarcinoma has a family history of colon cancer in her father (diagnosed at age 48) and colon cancer in her paternal aunt. Immunohistochemistry of her tumor demonstrates loss of MSH2 and MSH6 nuclear expression. What hereditary syndrome does she have?
items.exp: Lynch syndrome is an autosomal dominant condition caused by germline mutations in DNA mismatch repair (MMR) genes (MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2). Women with Lynch syndrome have a 40-60% lifetime risk of endometrial cancer (often presenting before age 50, preceding colon cancer) and a 40-60% lifetime risk of colorectal cancer.
r: Correct. MSH2/MSH6 loss with early-onset endometrial and colon cancer is diagnostic of Lynch syndrome.
Incorrect. Li-Fraumeni syndrome is caused by TP53 mutations causing sarcomas, breast, and brain tumors.
Incorrect. Cowden syndrome is caused by PTEN mutations causing hamartomas, breast, and thyroid cancer.
Incorrect. Peutz-Jeghers is caused by STK11 mutations causing GI hamartomas and mucocutaneous pigmentation.
items.kp: Lynch syndrome involves DNA mismatch repair deficiency (MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2) with high lifetime risks of endometrial and colon cancer.

items.q: Under the FIGO (2009/2018) staging system, a patient with endometrial adenocarcinoma has tumor invading through 65% of the myometrial thickness, but no cervical stromal invasion or extrauterine spread. What is the stage?
items.exp: FIGO Stage I endometrial carcinoma is confined to the uterine corpus: Stage IA is tumor limited to the endometrium or invading less than half (< 50%) of the myometrium; Stage IB is tumor invading half or more (>= 50%) of the myometrium.
r: Correct. Invasion >= 50% of the myometrial thickness without cervical or extrauterine spread is FIGO Stage IB.
Incorrect. Stage IA requires < 50% myometrial invasion.
Incorrect. Stage II requires invasion into cervical stroma.
Incorrect. Stage IIIC requires pelvic or para-aortic lymph node involvement.
items.kp: Endometrial carcinoma invading >= 50% of the myometrium is classified as FIGO Stage IB.

items.q: Which selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM) used in breast cancer treatment acts as an estrogen receptor agonist on the endometrium, increasing the relative risk of endometrial hyperplasia and adenocarcinoma 2- to 7-fold?
items.exp: Tamoxifen is a SERM that acts as an estrogen antagonist in breast tissue (inhibiting ER-positive breast cancer recurrence) but acts as a partial estrogen agonist in the uterus. Long-term tamoxifen therapy stimulates endometrial proliferation, increasing the risk of endometrial polyps, hyperplasia, and invasive endometrial carcinoma.
r: Correct. Tamoxifen exerts agonist effects on the endometrium, increasing endometrial cancer risk.
Incorrect. Raloxifene is an antagonist on the endometrium and does not increase cancer risk.
Incorrect. Anastrozole is an aromatase inhibitor, inducing hypoestrogenism.
Incorrect. Fulvestrant is a pure estrogen receptor down-regulator with no agonist activity.
items.kp: Tamoxifen acts as an estrogen agonist on the endometrium, increasing the risk of endometrial hyperplasia and cancer.

items.q: What is the standard surgical procedure for clinical Stage I endometrial carcinoma in an otherwise healthy patient?
o: Total laparoscopic hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy and sentinel lymph node biopsy
Radical abdominal hysterectomy with pelvic exenteration
Hysteroscopic tumor resection followed by pelvic radiation
items.exp: Minimally invasive total laparoscopic (or robotic) hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy (BSO) and sentinel lymph node (SLN) mapping (using indocyanine green cervical injection) is the international standard of care for apparent early-stage endometrial cancer, offering equivalent oncologic outcomes with lower morbidity than laparotomy.
r: Correct. Laparoscopic hysterectomy with BSO and sentinel node mapping is the evidence-based standard.
Incorrect. Radical hysterectomy and exenteration is overtreatment for Stage I disease.
Incorrect. Ovarian preservation is oncologically unsafe in postmenopausal endometrial cancer.
Incorrect. Hysteroscopic resection is not standard for invasive adenocarcinoma.
items.kp: Minimally invasive hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy and sentinel node mapping is standard for Stage I endometrial cancer.

items.q: A 68-year-old woman undergoes hysterectomy for uterine cancer. Final pathology shows uterine serous carcinoma invading only the inner 2 mm of myometrium, but peritoneal cytology is positive for malignant cells. How does uterine serous carcinoma differ biologically from endometrioid carcinoma?
o: It behaves aggressively with early transtubal peritoneal dissemination, regardless of myometrial invasion depth
It is completely curable by progestin therapy alone
It is estrogen-dependent and regresses after aromatase inhibitors
It never metastasizes to lymph nodes
items.exp: Uterine serous carcinoma (Type II) is biologically distinct from endometrioid cancer. It behaves aggressively like high-grade ovarian cancer, with a high propensity for early transtubal exfoliation, extensive peritoneal seeding, and distant lymph node metastases even when primary myometrial invasion is minimal or absent.
r: Correct. Uterine serous carcinoma has early propensity for peritoneal and nodal dissemination even without deep myometrial invasion.
Incorrect. Progestin therapy is ineffective in serous carcinoma due to lack of hormone receptors.
Incorrect. Serous carcinoma is estrogen-independent and p53-driven.
Incorrect. Lymph node metastasis rates exceed 30% even in clinically confined disease.
items.kp: Uterine serous carcinoma is an aggressive Type II tumor with early transtubal peritoneal spread regardless of myometrial depth.

items.q: Which molecular classification category defined by the Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) carries the most favorable prognosis in endometrial cancer, characterized by ultramutated DNA polymerase epsilon catalytic subunit mutations?
items.exp: The TCGA molecular classification defines four prognostic groups: POLE ultramutated (harboring exonuclease domain mutations in POLE, with exceptional progression-free survival near 100%); MSI-H (mismatch repair deficient, intermediate prognosis); Copy number low (microsatellite stable endometrioid, intermediate prognosis); and Copy number high (p53 abnormal, aggressive with poor prognosis).
r: Correct. POLE ultramutated tumors have an exceptionally favorable prognosis and rarely recur even without adjuvant therapy.
Incorrect. MSI-H has intermediate prognosis.
Incorrect. Copy number low has intermediate prognosis.
Incorrect. Copy number high (p53 abnormal) has the worst prognosis.
items.kp: POLE ultramutated endometrial cancers have an exceptionally favorable prognosis with near 100% survival.

items.q: What is the primary role of sentinel lymph node (SLN) mapping using indocyanine green (ICG) in early-stage endometrial cancer surgery?
o: Accurate nodal staging and detection of micrometastases while reducing lymphedema morbidity compared to full lymphadenectomy
Complete destruction of pelvic nerve plexuses
Eliminating the need for bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy
items.exp: Sentinel lymph node mapping (using cervical injection of indocyanine green) accurately identifies the first draining lymph nodes. Coupled with pathological ultrastaging (cytokeratin immunohistochemistry), it detects low-volume micrometastases with high sensitivity while dramatically reducing the incidence of lower extremity lymphedema associated with routine full pelvic and para-aortic lymphadenectomy.
r: Correct. SLN mapping provides accurate nodal staging and ultrastaging while minimizing lymphedema morbidity.
Incorrect. Nodal mapping does not treat hematogenous metastases.
Incorrect. Surgical technique aims to spare pelvic autonomic nerves.
Incorrect. BSO remains mandatory.
items.kp: Sentinel lymph node mapping provides accurate nodal staging with ultrastaging while reducing lymphedema compared to full dissection.

items.q: Which adjuvant therapy is indicated for a patient with Stage IA, Grade 1 endometrioid endometrial adenocarcinoma with no lymphovascular space invasion (LVSI)?
items.exp: Patients with Stage IA, Grade 1 endometrioid carcinoma without lymphovascular space invasion belong to the low-risk category. Their risk of recurrence is less than 3-5%, and multiple prospective randomized trials (GOG-99, PORTEC-1) have demonstrated no overall survival benefit from adjuvant radiation or chemotherapy. Observation alone is the standard of care.
r: Correct. Stage IA Grade 1 without LVSI is low-risk, requiring observation alone with no adjuvant therapy.
Incorrect. Pelvic radiation exposes the patient to toxicities without survival benefit.
Incorrect. Chemotherapy is overtreatment for low-risk disease.
Incorrect. Tamoxifen is not indicated and can promote endometrial proliferation.
items.kp: Low-risk endometrial cancer (Stage IA, Grade 1, no LVSI) requires surgical staging followed by observation alone.
